questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Karan said to us, “You should leave early for the airport so as to reach on time.”

options.text: Karan told us that we would leave early for the airport so as to reach on time.
Karan told us that we had to leave early for the airport so as to reach on time.
Karan told us to have left early for the airport so as to reach on time.
Karan told us that we should leave early for the airport so as to reach on time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 4.**

To change the sentence from direct to indirect speech, we need to make the following changes:

 
• **"Said" becomes "told"** as the given sentence is in the form of a statement.
 
• The tone of the sentence is **imperative**, hence the rest of the sentence **remains unchanged**. 

Option 1 is incorrect as the changed sentence contains the pronoun,** "we"**, which is not a suitable form of **"you"** when used in the indirect mode. The **verb "Should"** has been changed to **"would"**, which tampers with the meaning of the original sentence. 

Option 2 is incorrect as the verb **"should"** has been changed to **"had to"**, which as we have seen in the case of option 1, gives a whole **different meaning** to the sentence.

Option 3 is incorrect as the **verb has changed**. Moreover, we cannot use **"told" and "have left"** side-by-side as they are **verbs of different tenses**.

questions.question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

The teacher told us that we all were intelligent children but were not sincere in our work.

options.text: The teachers said to us, "You all were intelligent children but were not sincere in your work."
The teachers said to us, "We all are intelligent children but are not sincere in our work."
The teacher said to us, ‘‘We all are intelligent children but were not sincere in your work."
The teacher said to us, “You all are intelligent children but are not sincere in your work.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4.** In option 4, all verbs have been changed to their correct forms. **'Our' **has changed into** 'your'**.

Option 1 is** incorrect** as it uses 'were' in place of 'are' in the direct mode of narration

Option 2 is** incorrect** as it uses 'we' in place of 'you' and 'our' in place of 'your'

Option 3 is** incorrect **as it uses 'we' in place of 'you' and the usage of verbs is not consistent throughout the sentence. 

***When we convert a sentence from indirect to direct speech, we make the following changes***:

 
• **Quotation marks** are added and the sentence **ends with a full stop, comma or interrogation** mark depending on the **tone of the reported speech**.
 
• The **tense of the verb**, in the **reported speech** involving **any order, request and instruction **does **not** undergo **any change** during the conversion from indirect to direct mode. This is also true if the statement is a **universal truth**.
 
• If the **reporting verb** is in the present tense, it does not undergo any change.
 
• We omit the word **'to' **before the verb if the verb is in **bare infinitive.**
 
• When the reporting or** principal verb **is in the** past tense**, all past tenses of the indirect are changed into the corresponding **present tenses.**
 
• Words expressing **distance** are generally converted into into words expressing **nearness in time or place**. For eg. then becomes now, that day becomes today, that becomes this etc.
 
• In reporting **commands and requests**, the** verb **expressing command or request is **omitted** and the** infinitive** is changed into the **imperative**.
 
• In reporting **questions **the verbs like **asked, inquired** are omitted and** replaced** by **'said to'.**
 
• In reporting** exclamations and wishes**, the **verb **expressing exclamation or wish is omitted and simply replaced by** 'said'**

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

Yesterday, the farmers in Hathras rounded up about 25 abandoning cows and bulls and took them to a dairy in a truck.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'** i.e. **'about 25 abandoning cows'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the sentence is in the phrase** "about 25 abandoning cows"**. The word 'abandoning' is misused here.
 
• The **correct** term should be '**abandoned**' which means left by their owners.
 
• 'Abandoning' is the present participle form of 'abandon' and implies that an action is being done by the subject (in this case, the cows), which is not the intended meaning in this context.
 
• Here, 'abandoned' correctly implies that the cows and bulls were left unattended or deserted.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is 'about 25 abandoning cows'.

So the correct sentence should be: "Yesterday, the farmers in Hathras rounded up about 25 abandoned cows and bulls and took them to a dairy in a truck." [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abandoned: (त्यागा हुआ)** - Left without care or attention; deserted or forsaken.

 
 
• **Example:** The abandoned factory stood silent, a relic of the industrial past.

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

When we reached the beach, the fishermen were offloading the fish.

options.text: When we reached the beach, the fish were being offloaded by the fishermen.
When we reached the beach, the fish have been offloaded by the fishermen.
When we reached the beach, the fishermen were being offloaded by the fish.
When we reached the beach, the fish were offloading the fishermen.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1 i.e. *When we reached the beach, the fish were being offloaded by the fishermen.***

__Explanation__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e97c856a86e7f9a2254b6d21594beffe8b2a2afbb0c5bd00cd60b251c8f9881c.png] 

The given sentence is in the **active voice** and the **principal verb 'were'** is the **simple past** form of the** 'be'** verb

**Rules of Conversion from Active to Passive Voice:**

1. Identify the subject, the verb, and the object: S+V+O

2. Change the object into subject

3. Put the suitable helping verb or auxiliary verb according to the tense. 

4. Change the verb into past participle of the verb

5. Add the preposition "by“

6. Change the subject into object

7. Keep the manner(indefinite, continuous, perfect, perfect continuous) of the verb unchanged. 

**__Example:__**

__Active Voice:__** *Sameer wrote a letter. ***(Subject) + (verb) + (object).

__Passive Voice:__** *A letter was written by Sameer. ***(Object) + (auxiliary verb) + (past participle) + (by subject).

**Option 1** follows all the required rules of sentence transformation.

When we convert a sentence from indirect to direct speech, we make the following changes:

 
• **Quotation marks** are **added **and the sentence ends with a** full stop, comma or interrogation** mark depending on the** tone **of the reported speech.
 
• The **tense of the verb**, in the reported speech involving **any order, request and instruction** does not undergo any change during the conversion from indirect to direct mode. This is also true if the statement is a universal truth.
 
• If the **reporting verb** is in the** present or future tense**, it does not undergo any change.
 
• If the **reporting verb** of the indirect mode is in the past tense, the verb in the direct speech undergoes a backshift of tense.
 
• If the **verb in the reported speech** is in the present tense, the tense of that verb remains unchanged.

 We have to make the necessary changes during conversion.

• When we convert a sentence from the direct to the indirect mode(especially for a sentence** ending** with a** mark of interrogation**), we** reverse** the **subject-verb placement.** In **direct** sentences, we have the **verb before the subject**; while in** indirect,** the **verb follows the subject. **

questions.question:
**Given below are four sentences, three of which, are jumbled. Pick the option that gives the correct order.**

A. When I reached home, dinner was being served.

B. Still talking, he opened the matchbox, and a very annoyed scorpion came out of the box.

C. Having finished his meal my brother Larry brought cigarettes and in order to light one picked up a matchbox from the shelf.

D. I placed the matchbox with a scorpion in it on a shelf in the dining room and joined the family.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'ADCB'. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sentence A comes first as it introduces the situation when the author reached home.
 
• Sentence D follows A as it tells about where he placed the scorpion while having dinner.
 
• Sentence C follows D as it states that Larry (his brother) picked the matchbox from the shelf.
 
• Sentence B follows C as it mentions Larry's reaction on opening the matchbox.
 
• Thus, the sequence becomes:
 
 
• ​A: When I reached home, dinner was being served.
 
• D: I placed the matchbox with a scorpion in it on a shelf in the dining room and joined the family.
 
• C: Having finished his meal my brother Larry brought cigarettes and in order to light one picked up a matchbox from the shelf.
 
• B: Still talking, he opened the matchbox, and a very annoyed scorpion came out of the box.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the paragraph and eliminate the irrelevant options.
 
• Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences of the paragraph (concluding sentence).
 
• Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants. Identify the pronouns connecting the sentences with one other.

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

Anurag has been transferred to Mumbai.

options.text: They have transferred Anurag to Mumbai.
Anurag was transferring them to Mumbai.
They were transferring Anurag to Mumbai.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **They have transferred Anurag to Mumbai.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the passive voice and '**Anurag**' is the subject.
 
• When we convert this sentence into active voice, the subject 'Anurag' of the passive voice becomes the object.
 
• The passive format "have + been + V3 (transferred)" should be converted into the active format "have + V2 (transferred)" to account for the new subject-verb agreement
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the present perfect tense.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

**Subject 1+was/were+ being+ past participle + (by+agent)**

questions.question:
**Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.**

He told me that he had been late for the interview.

options.text: He said to me. “I was late for the interview.”
He said to me. ‘He had been late for the interview.”
He said to me, “He is being late for the interview.”
He said to me, “I was being late for the interview.”

questions.solution:
Given is a sentence written in **Indirect speech**, we need to **change it to Direct Speech. Option 1 is the right answer.**

While changing from **Indirect to Direct the Past Perfect changes to Simple Past Tense.**

The given sentence- He told me that he had been late for the interview.

**Subject + Reporting Verb + That + Reported Speech (Past Perfect).**

Will **get converted to**- He said to me. “I was late for the interview.”

**Subject + Reporting Verb + Reported Speech (Past Tense).**

So **Option 1** is the right answer as it changes the **past perfect-- 'had been late' to simple past tense - 'was late'. **

**Option 2 **uses the** third person-- He had been late** instead of the** 1st person I.**

**Option 3 **has the** present continuous-- is being late.**

**Option 4 **has the** past continuous-- was being late.**

**Option 1 is the right answer.**

__NOTE:__

We use **inverted commas (")** (also called quotation marks, quotes or speech marks) **to indicate direct speech.**

**A comma (,) **is used at the end of the quotation, before the closing speech mark.

A comma is also used before the quotation if we start the sentence with the reporting clause.

The **terminal full stop (.)** comes before the closing speech mark.

If the **quotation is a question or exclamation, the terminal marks (? and !)** also come before the closing speech marks.

The quotation normally **begins with a capital letter**, except if it is interrupted by a reporting clause, in which case the first letter of the continuation is not capitalised.

questions.question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

Did you hear what was said by her?

options.text: Did she hear what you said?
Did you hear what she has said?
Did you hear what she said?
Have you heard what she said?

questions.solution:
If you say **did you hear** (past tense) it means did you hear **at some point in the past? **

If you say **have you heard** (present perfect) it means did you hear **at some point in the recent past?**

**So as Option 3 **fulfills all the parameters of a **past tense that is in the given question**-- it is the right answer.

**Option 1** is incorrect as - you said - hints at **you saying something.**

**Option 2** is incorrect as -has said- has **a present perfect tense**

**Option 4 **is incorrect as -have you heard-- has **a present perfect tense**

**Option 3 is the correct active form of the given passive question.**

 

**Rules of Conversion from Active to Passive Voice:**

1. Identify the subject, the verb and the object: S+V+O

2. Change the object into subject

3. Put the suitable helping verb or auxiliary verb

4. Change the verb into past participle of the verb

5. Add the preposition "by“

6. Change the subject into object

7. The manner of the tense(indefinite, continuous, perfect, perfect continuous) remains unchanged. 

**__Example:__**

__Active Voice:__** *Sameer wrote a letter. ***(Subject) + (verb) + (object).

__Passive Voice:__** *A letter was written by Sameer. ***(Object) + (auxiliary verb) + (past participle) + (by subject).

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The given sentence speaks of an action that was taking place in the past and so should be in the form-- [was + being + past participle of the verb] at a particular time in the past, which had an effect on something else.

**The error is in option 3** [ repaired-- a simple past tense verb].
